title: Ankhorage Projects
summary: Provides standalone project identity, persistence, and repository-oriented project actions.
purpose: Offer a reusable boundary for storing, revising, materializing, and managing application project identities without coupling callers to a specific persistence provider.
responsibilities: Define actions for listing, reading, creating, updating, saving, reloading, materializing, and deleting persisted projects.
Preserve validated project manifests as immutable revisions.
Expose reusable project capabilities through published package entrypoints.
boundaries: Does not provide a concrete database, filesystem, or cloud persistence adapter.
Does not generate project output itself; materialization delegates through an injected owner generator.
Does not own application authoring UI, deployment, or source-repository provider implementations.
audience: Application and tooling authors that need portable project identity and revision actions.
Adapter authors that provide persistence or materialization implementations.
useCases: Persist a validated application manifest as a project revision.
Read project identity and revision history through a provider-neutral API.
Materialize a stored revision through an injected generator.

architecture.role: Provider-neutral project-domain library with public capabilities for project lifecycle actions.
invariants: Project revisions are immutable after persistence.
Provider-specific persistence and generation remain injected at package boundaries.
Consumers use declared published APIs rather than repository-local source imports.

limitations: A consumer must supply concrete persistence and generation behavior where those operations are required.
The package does not select or configure external storage providers.
